2. Respondent No.2 filed a complaint and based on that, a case came to be registered against the petitioners for the offences punishable under Sections 408, 420, 465 and 468 read with Section 34 NC: 2024:KHC-D:11844 of IPC in Kagwad Police Station Crime No.183/2022.
The said FIR and complaint are sought to be quashed in present petition.
3. I have heard the leaned counsel for the petitioners and the learned counsel for respondent No.2 and the learned Government Pleader for respondent No.1.

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel for the petitioners would contend that the complaint is dated 07.11.2022 and on going through the averments of the complaint that dates of alleged act between 03.11.2022 to 19.11.2022 itself indicate that subsequent period to the date of the complaint have been stated in the complaint.
He further contends that the alleged confession by the petitioners as noted in the averments of the complaint is on 19.11.2022 which is subsequent to the date of complaint.
On these grounds, he prayed to quash the proceedings against the petitioners.

Learned counsel for respondent No.2 would contend that considering the averments of the complaint that the period alleged regarding creating the fake receipts between 03.11.2022 to 19.11.2022 itself indicate that the date of complaint might be 07.12.2022 and there may be mistake in mentioning the month in the complaint and it could be seen that as the complaint is registered by the police on 08.12.2022 itself indicate that the complaint might be dated 07.12.2022.

He contends that on going though the averments of the complaint, there is an allegation of creating false receipts by the petitioners and getting benefit of the false receipts for themselves and causing loss to the factory.
The said averments of the complaint requires investigation.
Merely because there is mistake in mentioning the date is not a ground for quashing the proceedings.
With this, he prayed to dismiss the petition.

Learned High Court Government Pleader would contend that on perusal of the averments of the complaint, it is clear that there are serious allegations against the petitioners and it is only the investigation which will reveal what is the truth of the matter and involvement of the petitioners.
With this, she prayed to dismiss the petition.
7. Having heard the learned counsel, the Court has perused the averments of the complaint and the FIR.

8. Upon perusal of the averments of the complaint, it is clear that there are allegations of creating false receipts by these petitioners between 03.11.2022 to 19.11.2022 and they admitted the guilt committed by them.
It is also stated that the same has been recorded in CCTV Camera.
It is not in dispute that the petitioners were working in the sugar factory of respondent No.2 during the relevant NC: 2024:KHC-D:11844 period.

Considering the period mentioned i.e. 03.11.2022 to 19.11.2022 and the registration of the case on 08.12.2022 indicate that the complaint might be filed on 07.12.2022 and mistakenly the date is mentioned as 07.11.2022.
Considering the entire averments of the complaint, the matter requires investigation to ascertain the involvement of these petitioners.

Therefore, considering all these aspects, there are no grounds for quashing the FIR and complaint as prayed.
9.
In the result, the following ORDER The petition is dismissed.
